newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wesfarmers soars with nine-month results.
newsitem.headline: Wesfarmers soars with nine-month results.

text.p: Shares in Wesfarmers Ltd soared to a record high A$11.40 on Tuesday as the diversified agricultural and chemicals group posted a 51 percent increase in net profit to A$97 million for the nine months to March 31.
"It looked like a very strong result," said Hartley Poynton analyst, David Franklin, adding that the full year outlook was also buoyant.
"The profit of A$97 million implies that they made about A$40 million in the third quarter and I think you will see a general rerating upwards of earnings estimates," he said.

The company said it remained positive about the outlook for the full year result, expecting steady profit contributions from hardware retailing and gas and strong last quarter demand for cropping fertilisers and chemicals.

"We had an early break to the agricultural season in Western Australia that would have improved sales of fertiliser and that was one of the driving factors," agreed Franklin, although he noted an improved outlook for other arms of the company with efficiency gains and broader economic signals.

"Across all of the divisions it is looking quite good. You have productivity improvements in the coal business and also in the timber business, you have a cyclical recovery potentially in wool, beef and housing down the track and cost savings in Dalgety's," he said.
Since its 1996 year end close of A$8.80, Wesfarmer's shares have climbed nearly 30 percent to today's record levels.
Wesfarmers is about 51 percent owned by The Franked Income Fund whose units also reached a record high, up eight at A$3.35.
By 1.05 p.m. (0305 GMT), Wesfarmers shares were off their highs at A$11.35, still up 15.5 cents on the day, on turnover of 177,463 shares.
